results.quote: Let k=vc(G). In 2^{O(k log k)}(n+m) time, one can compute the minimum number of flips needed to reach a proper coloring, or determine that no proper q-coloring exists. In particular, Flip-CD is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by vc(G).
Let k=dtc(G). In 2^{O(k^2)} n^3 time, one can compute the minimum number of flips needed to reach a proper coloring, or determine that no proper q-coloring exists.
Swap-CD is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by vc(G)+q.
Flip-CD is W[1]-hard parameterized by td(G)+fvs(G).

results.bound: \text{W[1]-hard parameterized by } q+\mathrm{bw}(G) \text{ and by } q+\mathrm{ddp}(G)
results.quote: Each of Swap-CD and Slide-CD is W[1]-hard parameterized by q+bw(G) and by q+ddp(G). For the parameter q+ddp(G), hardness holds even on graphs with a dominating vertex, and hence on graphs of diameter at most two.

results.bound: \text{NP-complete on connected graphs with } q=4 \text{ and } \mathrm{diam}(G)=2; \text{ para-NP-complete parameterized by } q+\mathrm{diam}(G)
results.quote: For each of flipping, swapping, and sliding, Coloring Discovery is NP-complete on connected graphs of diameter exactly two, even with exactly four available colors. Consequently, on connected input graphs, each variant is para-NP-complete parameterized by q+diam(G), and also by q together with either radius or domination number.

results.bound: \text{no universal } \theta \text{ such that } O(\theta^{\mathrm{vc}(G)} n^{O(1)}) \text{ for all fixed } q, \text{ unless ETH fails}
results.quote: For each variant X\in\{\text{Flip-CD},\text{Swap-CD},\text{Slide-CD}\}, there is no universal constant \theta such that, for every fixed q, the restriction of X to q colors can be solved in O(\theta^{\mathrm{vc}(G)}n^{O(1)}) time, unless ETH fails.
